about: Sim Mill demo questions: the Paper Mill's own recycled-board mill, one modelled year ("today" Oct 31, 2026), generated by tools/sim-mill with The Paper Mill engine driving it (the-paper-mill sim-headless historian run: grades, sheet breaks, upsets, failures and the process tags; tools/sim-mill/engine/). Five planted faults (F1–F5, tools/sim-mill/config/plants.yaml); everything else is emergent. Each check runs through the same tool functions the assistant uses. Dates are written for the base year (Nov 1 2025 to Oct 31 2026); tools/sim-mill/run.py renders answer_key.json for the current 6-week cycle, filling {{…}} from the generated data.

questions.question: What should we prioritize for the Nov 11 outage?
questions.expect: Lead with the reel drum DS bearing: Bonvoy has flagged it since Jul 21, the Keel route confirmed an outer race defect on Aug 12 (0.17 in/s), it missed the Aug 19 outage because the bearing (22238 CCK/W33) wasn't in stores, and it read 0.39 in/s on the Oct 14 route (Danger is 0.40); the WO is in the Nov 11 scope waiting on parts, ETA Nov 5. Then both refiner plate changes (REF 1 due, REF 2 early because its plates are wearing fast) with only one Ridgeway set on hand, the 3rd section DS rotary joint replacement Brightwater recommends after three seal failures, and the two jobs with parts not reserved (couch roll seal strips, 2nd section PV fan belts).

checks.desc: Nov 11 scope has the reel drum DS bearing WO, waiting on parts
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_outage_scope(:org, 'OUT-2026-11-11') where description ilike '%reel drum DS bearing%' and status = 45 and parts_status = 'On order')

checks.desc: Bonvoy flagged the reel drum DS bearing on 20+ days from July
checks.sql: (select count(*) from public.mm_llm_bonvoy(:org, 'PM1:REEL_DRUM_DS_VIB', '2026-07-01', '2026-10-31')) >= 20

checks.desc: the Aug 12 vibration route is found for "reel drum outer race defect"
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_search_docs(:org, 'reel drum outer race defect', 3) where doc_id = 'KV-VR-260812')

checks.desc: both refiner plate changes are in the Nov 11 scope with parts not reserved
checks.sql: (select count(*) from public.mm_llm_outage_scope(:org, 'OUT-2026-11-11') where description in ('Change REF 1 refiner plates', 'Change REF 2 refiner plates') and parts_status = 'Not reserved') = 2

questions.question: Why did we change the 2nd press top felt early in May?
questions.expect: It filled in about three weeks: Uhle box vacuum climbed from late April (Bonvoy flagged it from May 10), press solids fell and the 4th section steam hit its limit on 34 Super, holding speed back. The Spraywell audit on May 13 found 22% of the 2nd press top HP shower nozzles plugged and the supply strainer packed. The felt came out on May 19 after 34 days (target 42) in a 7.5 h shut; Marlow's analysis found 71% fill. RCFA-SM-26-008 is still open: the action to add Uhle vacuum rate of rise to Bonvoy is overdue.

checks.desc: the felt is an early removal (34 days of 42, reason performance)
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_position_life(:org, 'p2-felt-top') where removed = '2026-05-19' and early and reason = 'performance')

checks.desc: Bonvoy flagged the 2nd press top Uhle vacuum in May
checks.sql: (select count(*) from public.mm_llm_bonvoy(:org, 'PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC', '2026-05-01', '2026-05-19')) >= 3

checks.desc: the May 13 shower audit is found for "nozzles plugged 2nd press top felt"
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_search_docs(:org, 'nozzles plugged 2nd press top felt', 3) where doc_id = 'SW-SA-260513')

checks.desc: its RCFA still has an overdue action
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_rcfa_status(:org, '2026-10-31') where title ilike '%2nd press top felt%' and overdue >= 1)

questions.question: Overlay Uhle vacuum on the 2nd press top felt for the April felt against the two felts before it, by days on the machine.
questions.expect: The Apr 15 felt tracks the Jan 21 and Mar 4 felts for about two weeks (all around 9.5–10 inHg), then pulls away from about day 14–17: roughly 11.9 inHg at day 25 against about 10.5 for the other two, and 14.4 inHg at day 33, the day before it came out on May 19. The earlier felts were still near 11 inHg at day 33 and ran their full 41 days, ending near 11.8. Chart: three lines on a shared Day 1… axis.

checks.desc: the Jan 21, Mar 4 and Apr 15 felt runs are on file
checks.sql: (select count(*) from public.mm_llm_position_life(:org, 'p2-felt-top') where installed in ('2026-01-21', '2026-03-04', '2026-04-15')) = 3

checks.desc: at day 33 the April felt reads 2+ inHg above the March felt
checks.sql: (select avg from public.mm_llm_pi_daily(:org, 'PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC', '2026-05-18', '2026-05-18')) > (select avg from public.mm_llm_pi_daily(:org, 'PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC', '2026-04-06', '2026-04-06')) + 2

questions.question: Did the May 19 felt change fix the press? Chart the week before against the week after.
questions.expect: Yes. Week before (May 12–18) against week after (May 20–26): Uhle vacuum about 13.6 → 9.5 inHg, press exit solids 42.5 → 44.0%, 4th section steam 126 → 117 psig (off its limit), speed about 2,170 → 2,310 fpm, sheet breaks 22 → 5, and about 686 → 729 t a day. The press was back to its early-April numbers within the week. Chart: before and after for each measure.

checks.desc: Uhle vacuum fell 3+ inHg after the change
checks.sql: (select avg(avg) from public.mm_llm_pi_daily(:org, 'PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC', '2026-05-12', '2026-05-18')) - (select avg(avg) from public.mm_llm_pi_daily(:org, 'PM1:UHLE_P2T_VAC', '2026-05-20', '2026-05-26')) > 3

checks.desc: press solids rose and breaks fell
checks.sql: (select avg(avg) from public.mm_llm_pi_daily(:org, 'PM1:PRESS_SOLIDS', '2026-05-20', '2026-05-26')) > (select avg(avg) from public.mm_llm_pi_daily(:org, 'PM1:PRESS_SOLIDS', '2026-05-12', '2026-05-18')) and (select sum(breaks) from public.mm_llm_production(:org, '2026-05-20', '2026-05-26', 'day')) < (select sum(breaks) from public.mm_llm_production(:org, '2026-05-12', '2026-05-18', 'day'))

Both plate sets are due on Nov 11 and there is one Ridgeway set on hand, so the second set needs ordering now (that action is overdue). questions.question: Did the 3rd section syphon differential warn us before each rotary joint leak? Show the 10 days before each one.
questions.expect: Clearly for two of the three, by a few days; October is muddied by the Sep 30 outage. The differential normally sits around 4.1–4.3 psi and dropped to about 3.1–3.3 psi before each seal failure: from about Dec 31 before the Jan 6 leak, from about Jun 20 before Jun 23, and from about Oct 1 before Oct 2, after a smaller dip around Sep 21–25 (Sep 30 reads low because of the outage, not the joint). Bonvoy flagged it 2, 3 and 1 days ahead. That is enough warning to plan the seal change, and with three failures and no RCFA the joint should be replaced on Nov 11. Chart: three lines aligned on days before each leak.

checks.desc: three unplanned stops on the 3rd section DS rotary joint
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_repeat_stops(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31') where equipment = '3rd section rotary joint (DS)' and events = 3)

checks.desc: Bonvoy flagged the differential in the days before the Jan 6 and Jun 23 leaks
checks.sql: (select count(*) from public.mm_llm_bonvoy(:org, 'PM1:DRY3_DP', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-06')) >= 1 and (select count(*) from public.mm_llm_bonvoy(:org, 'PM1:DRY3_DP', '2026-06-18', '2026-06-23')) >= 1

questions.question: Which repeat failures don't have an RCFA?
questions.expect: The 3rd section DS rotary joint: three steam leaks (Jan 6, Jun 23, Oct 2), about 8 h down in all, each under the 3 h RCFA threshold and more than 60 days apart, so none triggered an RCFA. Bonvoy saw the 3rd section syphon differential drop for days before each one. Brightwater's Oct 14 survey says the joint is misaligned on its bracket and seal kits alone will keep failing: replace and re-align it at the next outage. (The headbox slime stops and the forming fabric stops repeat too, but each has RCFAs.)

checks.desc: repeat stops: the 3rd section DS rotary joint, 3 stops, no RCFA
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_repeat_stops(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31') where equipment = '3rd section rotary joint (DS)' and events = 3 and rcfas = 'none')

questions.question: Is the reel drum bearing temperature following the vibration? Plot both since mid-July.
questions.expect: Yes. Both were flat until late July and have climbed together since: vibration from about 0.06 to about 0.43 in/s on Oct 31 (past Danger at 0.40) and DS bearing temperature from about 134 to about 168 °F. Neither has levelled off, which fits the outer race defect the Keel route found on Aug 12 getting worse. The change is in the Nov 11 scope with the bearing on order. Chart: vibration on the left axis, temperature on the right, the 0.40 Danger line marked.

questions.question: Do we break more on 24# than on 34 Super? Chart it.
questions.expect: Yes, but by less than the raw counts suggest. 24# has 402 of the 578 breaks (70%), but it also ran 64% of the hours (about 5,600 h). Per 100 h run: 24# 7.2, 28# 6.7 (only 238 h, so a small sample), 31# 6.1 and 34 Super 5.2. So 24# breaks about 40% more often per hour than 34 Super. Chart: breaks per 100 h by grade.

checks.desc: 24# has 65%+ of the breaks but under 70% of the hours
checks.sql: (select share_pct from public.mm_llm_downtime_summary(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31', 'grade') where kind = 'break' and grp = '24#') >= 65 and (select share_pct from public.mm_llm_grade_hours(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31') where grade = '24#') < 70

checks.desc: 24# breaks more per 100 h than 34 Super
checks.sql: (select b.events / h.hours from public.mm_llm_downtime_summary(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31', 'grade') b join public.mm_llm_grade_hours(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31') h on h.grade = b.grp where b.kind = 'break' and b.grp = '24#') > (select b.events / h.hours from public.mm_llm_downtime_summary(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31', 'grade') b join public.mm_llm_grade_hours(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31') h on h.grade = b.grp where b.kind = 'break' and b.grp = '34 Super')

questions.question: Is one crew breaking more than the others? Show it on a chart.
questions.expect: B has the most breaks (164) and A the fewest (122), with C 147 and D 145. On DuPont 12 the four crews work the same hours, so the counts compare directly. B against A alone is a real-looking gap (about 2.5 standard deviations), but across all four crews the spread is close to what chance gives (chi-square p about 0.1). Worth watching, not proof of a crew problem; grade mix on each crew's shifts is the next thing to check. Chart: breaks by crew.

checks.desc: B has the most breaks and A the fewest
checks.sql: (select grp from public.mm_llm_downtime_summary(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31', 'crew') where kind = 'break' order by events desc limit 1) = 'B' and (select grp from public.mm_llm_downtime_summary(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31', 'crew') where kind = 'break' order by events limit 1) = 'A'

questions.question: Make a monthly chart of tons and break hours. Which month hurt most, and why?
questions.expect: Tons run about 20,500–21,700 a month (fewer in February, a short month). May was the worst month for breaks: 73 breaks and about 52 h of sheet-off time, with tons down to about 670 a day. That was the 2nd press top felt filling: Uhle vacuum up, the 4th section steam at its limit on 34 Super holding speed back, until the unplanned felt change on May 19. March had the lowest uptime (94.7%) from unplanned stops. Charts: tons by month and break hours by month (or one chart with two axes).

checks.desc: May has the most breaks
checks.sql: (select period from public.mm_llm_production(:org, '2025-11-01', '2026-10-31', 'month') order by breaks desc limit 1) = '2026-05'

checks.desc: the 2nd press top felt came out early in May
checks.sql: exists (select 1 from public.mm_llm_position_life(:org, 'p2-felt-top') where removed = '2026-05-19' and early)
